questions.stem: CASELET: A company has 1,200 employees in total. 40 % are women. 30 % of the men and 25 % of the women are married. Q: How many UNMARRIED employees does the company have?
questions.explanation: Women = 40 % × 1200 = 480. Men = 720. Married men = 30 % × 720 = 216. Married women = 25 % × 480 = 120. Total married = 336. Unmarried = 1200 − 336 = 864. Multi-step caselet item typical of Bank PO mains.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: CASELET (cont.): Using the figures above, what is the ratio of unmarried men to unmarried women?
questions.explanation: Unmarried men = 720 − 216 = 504. Unmarried women = 480 − 120 = 360. Ratio 504 : 360 = 21 : 15 (divide both by 24).
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: CASELET: In a school, the ratio of boys to girls is 7 : 5. 60 % of the boys and 40 % of the girls play a sport. If 180 girls DO NOT play a sport, find the total number of students.
questions.explanation: Girls not playing = 60 % of girls = 180 → girls total = 300. Ratio 7:5 → boys = 300 × 7/5 = 420. Total = 720.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: CASELET (cont.): In the same school, how many students in total play a sport?
questions.explanation: Boys playing = 60 % × 420 = 252. Girls playing = 40 % × 300 = 120. Total = 372. Independent second question that forces the student to re-use the caselet numbers.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: CASELET: Three candidates A, B, C stood in an election. A got 35 % of the valid votes and B got 45 %. The remainder went to C. If C received 3,600 votes, total valid votes were:
questions.explanation: A + B = 80 % → C = 20 % of valid = 3600 → valid = 18,000. If the question had asked for TOTAL votes (including invalid), an extra step would be needed; as stated it is valid-only.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
